For a nation or large corporation, this may involve complex legal and financial procedures.

  2. Wealth Transfer: This usually refers to transferring wealth from the rich or specific industries to the government or the broader public through tax policies or other means, in order to help repay public debt or support economic recovery. This practice may cause controversy among different social classes.

  3. Spending Cuts: Governments or individuals reduce non-essential expenditures, using the saved funds to repay debt. For governments, this may mean reducing investment in public services and social welfare; for individuals or families, it means reducing daily consumption.

  4. Printing More Currency (Inflation): Although it looks simple on the surface, in reality, this is done by increasing the money supply to dilute the real value of the debt. This method may lead to an increase in the inflation rate, subsequently affecting economic stability and purchasing power.

A Reflection

It took me several months to truly realize something so simple and familiar. Perhaps that is the meaning of them inventing new words. To take something you are very familiar with and make it something you don’t understand at all. If you understand a thing very well, then there is no room for maneuver.

item.title: My first speculative attempt
item.description: Will a conscious speculation be a lesson?
item.content:encoded:
My First Speculative Attempt

Operation Overview

This afternoon, I executed trades in my A-share account, selling 50% of my Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) shares.

Trading Logic

Today, small-cap stocks experienced an overall decline, while large-cap blue-chip stocks rose by 4% to 5%. Concurrently, the Ministry of Finance announced a press conference scheduled for Saturday. My analysis suggests that policymakers intend to temporarily stabilize the market by boosting large-cap stocks and enhancing market confidence by releasing relevant news. I predict that actual policies will be announced at the Saturday press conference to drive market recovery. Considering that the policymakers’ goals have not yet been achieved, I believe they will not abandon their intervention in the market.

Specific Trading Process

Based on the analysis above, I decided to sell in batches today and tomorrow, selling 50% of the current holding each time. At the same time, I plan to gradually buy back these shares on Monday and Tuesday of next week.

Reflection and Lessons Learned

This operation went against my most important principle: Don’t try to time the market. However, I want to test whether my recent understanding is correct through practical application. At the same time, I must admit that a profit-seeking mindset was intertwined with this operation. This experience made me realize that speculation is not just a test of the market, but also a test of one’s own emotions and judgment.

AI Evaluation of This Operation

From this journal entry, we can analyze the author’s mindset and behavior as follows:

Analytical Ability

The author demonstrates keen observation and analytical ability regarding market trends. He noticed the phenomenon of small-cap stocks declining and large-cap stocks rising, and attempted to link this to government policy to understand the underlying market drivers.

Decision-Making Process

Based on his analysis, the author made a short-term investment decision—selling a portion of his holdings and planning to repurchase them within the next few days. This indicates that he is attempting to profit from short-term market fluctuations.

Self-Awareness

The author realized that this operation violated one of his important principles—not trying to time the market. This shows a clear understanding of his investment strategy and a strong emphasis on adhering to principles.

Curiosity and Self-Verification

Despite violating the principle, the author decided to proceed with this operation, partly because he wanted to verify his market judgment. This reflects a certain curiosity and a spirit of self-challenge.

Greedy Mindset

The author frankly admitted that besides verifying his judgment, the desire to make money drove him to make this decision. This candor shows a clear recognition of his own motivations.

Risk Management

Although the author decided to engage in market timing, he adopted a strategy of selling in batches, selling only 50% of the holding each time. This indicates that while taking risks, he is also attempting to control them.

Self-Reflection

By recording this decision-making process and his thoughts, the author demonstrates a degree of self-reflection. He clearly recognizes the contradiction between his actions and his principles, which may help him make better decisions in the future.

Overall, this investor exhibits analytical ability, decision-making ability, self-awareness, curiosity, and risk management awareness, but also shows a certain degree of speculative psychology. His behavior reflects a common psychological conflict among investors—seeking balance between adhering to long-term principles and seizing short-term opportunities. This experience may become a valuable learning experience in his investment journey.

Areas for Improvement

  • Adherence to Principles: Professional investors need clear investment principles and must stick to them. His violation of his important principle may lead to unstable investment performance.
  • Emotional Control: Admitting the desire for profit, professional investors need to better control this emotion to prevent it from influencing judgment.
  • Short-term Trading Tendency: Attempting to time the market is a strategy that many professional investors struggle to succeed with long-term. More attention should be paid to long-term value.
  • Verification Method: While using “real money” to test one’s cognition is direct, it can be high-risk. Professional investors usually use more systematic and risk-controlled methods to verify investment hypotheses.

Recommendations

  1. Establish stricter investment discipline to avoid violating important principles set by oneself.
  2. Develop a more systematic risk management strategy.
  3. Try establishing a simulated investment account to test investment ideas, rather than using actual funds directly.
  4. Focus more on long-term investment strategies and reduce attention to short-term market fluctuations.
  5. Continue to maintain the habit of analyzing the market and self-reflecting, but focus more on translating these analyses into sustainable investment strategies.

What Happened Today?

According to reports from the Securities Times, on October 9th, the two major A-share markets showed a weak downward trend, accelerating into a plunge at the close of trading. The Shanghai Composite Index (SSE) fell sharply by nearly 7%, losing the 3300 point threshold, while the ChiNext Index (GEM) dropped by over 10%. The total trading volume of the two markets exceeded 2.9 trillion yuan, and over 5,000 individual stocks declined.

Reasons for the Surge

Regarding the previous market surge, I have already provided analysis in an earlier article. Interested readers can read the article

《A Historic Surge Day in A-Shares: False Prosperity or Steady Ascent?》 for further details.

The Essence of This Plunge

To understand the underlying reasons for this plunge, we first need to review several key assumptions:

  1. The Goal of Policymakers: To prevent the economy from falling into an asset-liability recession similar to the Great Depression, decision-makers chose to rescue the economy through monetary policy.
  2. The Stock Market as a Policy Tool: The central bank drove the stock market up by purchasing large volumes of shares, creating an asset bubble, and helping enterprises obtain liquidity.
  3. Inflation and Capital Flow: Policymakers hoped that inflation would force bank depositors to withdraw their savings from banks and invest them in other economic sectors, thereby helping the economy escape deflation. Since these policy tools were implemented, the market has seen significant short-term gains. However, today’s plunge signifies that the policy effects are being tested by market reality.

The Actual Situation in Today’s Market

Today, A-shares plunged 6% after opening, but looking at the overall situation, investors’ losses have not yet materialized. This is because the stock market has already risen by about 20% over the past two weeks, partially mitigating the impact of the short-term decline.

More notably, many veteran investors who experienced the 2016 stock market crash have still not entered the market. The veteran investors in a certain automotive sector that I have been closely monitoring remain cautious, showing a high level of vigilance toward the stock market. This phenomenon indicates that despite the short-term rapid rise and sudden fall in the market, the psychological trauma caused by the historic crash has not dissipated, and investor confidence has not yet recovered.

The cautious attitude of these veteran investors suggests that short-term market volatility is not enough to overcome their concerns about the market fundamentals. Speculative sentiment is rampant in the market, with many adopting a “make a quick profit and leave” mindset, because most people generally believe that the economic fundamentals have not fundamentally improved.

Analysis of the Plunge Causes

Today’s plunge was primarily driven by two factors:

  1. Realization of Prior Gains: After the market rose significantly, some investors chose to take profits at this time.
  2. Policy Below Expectations: The new policy announced yesterday was far below market expectations, leading to a shift in market sentiment toward pessimism and exacerbating today’s decline.

Future Outlook

I do not believe that this round of market volatility signifies the end of the upward trend. On the contrary, this may just be the beginning of a new cycle of fluctuations. Under the manipulation of policy and capital, the market is likely to continue rising amidst volatility. This is the strategy adopted by decision-makers to achieve their economic goals.

Although the central bank’s policies are not omnipotent in the long run, in the medium to short term, the central bank’s policies and capital support have a decisive impact on market direction. Therefore, we may see more similar fluctuations and reversals in the future.

item.title: Witnessing A-shares hit the limit up at the open
item.description: A-shares collectively surge! The Shanghai Composite Index opened up by over 10%, the ChiNext Board surged by 18.44%, and over a thousand stocks in the entire market rose by more than 19%.
item.content:encoded:
A Day of Witnessing Miracles

Today, the Shanghai Composite Index (SSE) opened 10% higher, but immediately slid downwards, ultimately closing up 4.59%, settling at 3489 points. The total trading volume of the two markets reached a massive 3.45 trillion yuan, setting a new historical high. What is particularly striking is that at the opening, almost all stocks touched the upper limit (limit-up), regardless of whether their performance was good or bad, or how high their P/E ratio was. This market trend can be described as a peculiar phenomenon unseen in decades.

Questions Behind the Miracle

Behind this phenomenon, we cannot help but ask:

  1. Has the economy truly begun to recover?
  2. Has the business environment improved?
  3. Has investment started to accelerate?
  4. Has consumer willingness increased?

Clearly, the answer is no. The market frenzy does not stem from a substantial improvement in economic fundamentals, but rather appears to be the result of human intervention.

Has the Market Reached a Phase Peak?

The market currently seems to have reached a phase peak, but this does not mean the upward trend will immediately end. In fact, the driving force behind this round of market activity is far more than just market sentiment; it is more complex, involving multiple economic and policy factors.

The Fundamental Reason for This Market Uptick

Since the economy peaked in 2022, the Chinese economy has gradually entered a deflationary channel. The Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) for manufacturing has continuously remained in the contraction range below 50, total social retail sales growth has stagnated, and the real estate market bubble has begun to burst. Even though some cities have lifted purchase restrictions and banks have lowered down payments to 15%, real estate prices have still fallen by an average of about 30% over the past two years. Consequently, local government land finance has suffered a severe blow.

At the same time, the youth unemployment rate has soared to 18%, and the pressure of local government debt is growing increasingly severe. Faced with such a grim economic situation, relying solely on the slogan of “singing a good economy” is no longer enough to reverse the decline; monetary and fiscal policies must be utilized to alleviate the local fiscal crisis and the youth unemployment problem.

On September 24th, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) implemented interest rate cuts and reserve requirement ratio cuts, and provided liquidity support to securities, fund, and insurance companies through a repurchase mechanism. These financial institutions exchanged high-liquidity assets, such as government bonds and central bank bills, for the liquidity required by the market, thereby stabilizing the stock market.

These policy measures directly drove the stock market up, creating a round of stock market asset bubble. Listed companies thus gained ample capital liquidity, and local governments can also alleviate debt pressure by selling shares of state-owned enterprises. Individual investors participated in this, gaining asset appreciation while also driving consumer recovery, providing short-term momentum for the economy to escape stagnation.

The Market’s Next Trend

After a week of trading, funds that entered the market early began realizing profits, leading to the market’s high open and low close today. Simultaneously, the Hong Kong stock market has also started to decline. Does this mean the market euphoria is about to end?

I believe that although the market may experience volatility in the short term, the fundamental driving force of this round of activity—the support from monetary and fiscal policies—has not ended. Therefore, the market’s upward trend may continue. To achieve its economic and policy goals, the government may introduce more easing policies, further increasing support for the market and continuing to drive the stock market higher.

Summary

The current market prosperity is exciting on the surface, but in the long run, an over-rise detached from economic fundamentals is ultimately difficult to sustain.

item.title: Relatively safe assets under severe inflation
item.description:
During hyperinflation, currency rapidly depreciates, leading to a sharp decline in purchasing power. To protect wealth in this environment, the following assets are usually considered relatively safe:

Precious Metals

Gold and silver have historically been viewed as hedges against inflation. Their intrinsic value is unaffected by specific monetary systems, and they often maintain or even increase their value during economic instability.

Real Assets

Real assets such as real estate, farmland, and forests can usually preserve value, and even appreciate during periods of hyperinflation. These assets not only have practical uses but can also generate rent or agricultural income.

Cryptocurrencies

In some cases, cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin are viewed as a tool against inflation because of their limited supply and lack of direct influence from government policies. However, the cryptocurrency market is highly volatile, requiring cautious investment.

Inflation-Protected Bonds

In some countries, government-issued inflation-protected bonds (such as TIPS in the US) are linked to the inflation index, providing protection.

Stocks

Stocks in certain industries, such as commodity producers, energy companies, and other businesses related to basic resources, may perform well during inflation because they can pass rising costs onto consumers.

Commodities

Commodities such as oil, natural gas, and grain often see price increases during inflation. Investing in these commodities can hedge against inflation risk.

Collectibles

Collectibles such as artworks, antiques, and luxury watches, which have intrinsic value and relatively independent markets, may maintain their value during hyperinflation.

Historical Lessons

This situation is bound to lead to extreme changes, which is unacceptable, so countermeasures must be taken. What is the goal of these countermeasures? Naturally, it is to maintain social stability, and on this point, everyone’s interests are aligned.

Current Solutions

1. Monetary Policy Intervention

  • Quantitative Easing (QE): They can instruct the central bank to inject large-scale currency, increasing market liquidity. This approach can rapidly boost asset prices, stimulate consumption, and create the illusion of economic prosperity.
  • Lowering Interest Rates: By lowering interest rates, they encourage borrowing by individuals and corporations, promoting investment and consumption, thereby stimulating economic activity.

2. Fiscal Policy Stimulus

  • Increasing Government Spending: They can increase spending through government projects and infrastructure construction to create jobs and promote economic growth. This investment can yield quick results and enhance public support for the government.
  • Tax Reduction: Reducing the tax burden in the short term increases disposable income for consumers, stimulating consumption and thereby promoting economic growth.

3. Market Manipulation

  • Stock Market Manipulation: By various means (e.g., the central bank directly purchasing stocks) to lift the stock market, creating a wealth effect, making the middle class and asset holders feel wealthy, thereby increasing consumption and investment.
  • Real Estate Market Stimulation: Lowering mortgage interest rates or providing housing subsidies to promote the recovery of the real estate market, thereby driving the development of related industries.

4. Information Manipulation

  • Propaganda and Public Opinion Control: Shaping a positive economic image through the propaganda machine, reducing public attention to economic problems, and enhancing public trust and support for the government.
  • Data Manipulation: Manipulating economic indicators and releasing optimistic economic data to create the illusion of economic prosperity.

5. Suppressing Social Dissatisfaction

  • Suppressing Dissenting Voices: By severely suppressing protests and opposition parties, maintaining surface-level social stability, and preventing the outbreak of social unrest and dissatisfaction.
  • Providing Short-Term Welfare: Providing some short-term economic aid or subsidies to low-income groups to alleviate livelihood pressure and gain public support.

6. Increasing State Control

Nationalization or Control of Key Industries: Achieving national interests and regime stability by controlling key economic sectors. This can help them better cope with crises during economic difficulties.

Conclusion Through these short-term or medium-term strategies, they can effectively maintain superficial prosperity and stability during an economic recession, strengthening their foundation of rule.

item.title: A Reflection on the Historic Surge of A-Shares: False Prosperity or Steady Ascent?
item.description: The Largest Single Day Surge in the History of China's Stock Market
item.content:encoded:
The Shanghai Composite Index surged by 8.06% today, breaking the 3300 point barrier. Trading volume across both markets reached a massive 2.6 trillion yuan, setting a new historical high. All stock brokerage stocks hit the upper limit (limit up). Faced with such a fierce rally, many people cannot help but wonder: How long can this crazy surge last? Should we take profits now?

Personally, I believe that this market trend is unlikely to be a fleeting phenomenon; rather, it is a medium-term process that may last for two or three months.

What exactly happened in today’s market?

Today, the three major A-share indices opened and rose collectively. The Shanghai Composite Index closed up 8.06%, standing above 3300 points; the Shenzhen Component Index rose 10.67%; and the ChiNext Index rose 15.36%. Furthermore, the Beijing Stock Exchange 50 and the STAR 50 rose by 22.84% and 17.88% respectively, both setting new records for the largest single-day gains. The total trading volume reached 259.3 billion yuan, an increase of over 114.7 billion yuan compared to the previous trading day. Although there was a net outflow of 51.7 billion yuan in capital from the overall market, the market presented a broad-based rally—5,336 stocks rose, only 8 fell, 713 stocks hit the upper limit, and 2 stocks hit the lower limit.

The various faces in the market

Today, I observed the reactions of various participants. There is a significant polarization between market newcomers and veterans.

Many market veterans are still in a wait-and-see attitude. Few people have actually entered the market, and those who have entered hold relatively small positions. Their thinking is that this wave of ascent is unsustainable, and a massive crash could happen tomorrow. Therefore, their trading style is quick in and quick out—making a quick profit and leaving.

In contrast, new investors who are experiencing such a massive surge for the first time are generally optimistic, even blindly so. They lack risk awareness. Continuous profits make them overly confident, believing they can make a huge profit in the stock market and walk away unscathed.

Why is the market so frenzied?

First, it must be said that this is the largest single-day gain I have witnessed. Today, various online groups have been bustling with activity, with both bulls and bears being extremely active. People’s attention to the stock market has reached a new height. Since the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) announced its personal intervention to purchase financial assets on September 24th:

  • Capital Inflow: A large amount of capital, lacking investment targets, poured into the A-share market, directly driving up the market.
  • Short Covering: As the market rose at an extremely fast pace, a large number of short sellers who used margin financing were forced to cover their positions, further pushing the market higher.
  • New Blood: The market has gone 8 years without a period of prosperity, and a new generation of young people who have never experienced a stock market boom are now ready to enter.

How is this market rise different from before?

Unlike in the past, I believe this time’s rise has clear distinctions from previous ones:

  • PBOC’s Personal Intervention: This time, the PBOC is not merely guiding policy; it is personally purchasing financial assets and establishing two structural monetary policy tools: the swap facility for securities, funds, and insurance companies, as well as stock repurchases and increased lending for share purchases. This scale of capital injection is unprecedented.

  • Clear Policy Direction: This rise is not simply a “harvesting of韭菜” (cutting leeks/profiteering on retail investors); rather, it is aimed at driving the prosperity of financial assets, which in turn pushes sectors like real estate, thereby alleviating downward economic pressure. This goal clearly requires a medium-to-long-term market rise, not just short-term volatility.

What will the future trend be?

Due to the public holiday, the market will be closed for 7 days starting tomorrow. After the holiday, the market may first experience a wave of correction, as many people hope to realize their paper profits. This is human nature—people prefer certain returns and crave the security of having profits in hand.

However, they will find that after a short-term market correction, the market will advance further upward, which is determined by the goals of this round of stimulus. Those who exited the market after realizing profits will be distressed by the market’s continuous climb, feeling that they cut off their gains too early. Consequently, some people will re-enter the market, and they will do so with even larger amounts of capital (just as Newton, the founder of physics, did during the stock market bubble).

Next, the market will reach a state of artificial prosperity. However, this prosperity certainly cannot last indefinitely.

  • Firstly, the fundamental economic conditions have not improved, and personal incomes have not increased. Although those holding financial assets have gained returns, the economy of the vast majority of people remains far from optimistic.
  • Secondly, real estate is facing huge inventory pressure. With only 8 million newborns this year, real estate cannot truly gain support from demand.

Ultimately, the artificial prosperity built upon strong stimulus will gradually cool down.

Conclusion

Behind today’s massive surge in the A-share market, the PBOC’s direct intervention is undoubtedly the key driving factor, and the reactions of different groups in the market have further amplified the market volatility. Although this rise has brought significant market prosperity in the short term, from a macroeconomic and structural perspective, this prosperity carries great uncertainty. The market may experience a correction after the holiday, followed by continued upward movement driven by policy, potentially entering a state of artificial prosperity. However, the pressure from the fundamental economy and the real estate market will eventually cause the market heat to cool down.

On September 24, 2024, the Central Bank held a press conference and announced a new round of economic stimulus plan, which aims to inject approximately 300 billion yuan into the stock market, stating that further capital injections will continue in the future. Overall, this strategy appears quite well-planned; by boosting the stock market, the intention is to guide residents directly into financial market investments. This measure may attract a large influx of funds into the market in the short term, bringing about short-term prosperity. However, the sustainability of this effect remains questionable.

Motives Behind the Economic Stimulus

Why launch a new round of stimulus policy at this time? I believe the main reason is the continuous deterioration of the economic situation. It seems unlikely that the government can achieve the 5% GDP growth target this year, and this move appears to be a last-ditch effort.

As a large amount of capital enters the stock market, a wave of upward momentum is indeed possible. The overall capital volume in the current A-share market is not large, so this massive injection of funds can certainly push up the stock market in the short term. However, how long it can be sustained depends on the intensity of subsequent policies and the determination of the decision-makers.

Long-Term Economic Fundamentals Still Face Challenges

Although the stock market may rise in the short term, from a long-term perspective, the economic fundamentals have not fundamentally changed, and specific problems still exist:

  • Corporate profit margins are continuously declining
  • Unemployment rate has not shown significant improvement
  • The “only rising, never falling” myth of the real estate market has been shattered
  • Heavily indebted homeowners are not keen on taking on more leverage

From an economic perspective, when an economy faces a recession, interest rate cuts are usually seen as an effective means of stimulating market vitality and promoting economic growth. However, the effectiveness of interest rate cuts relies on businesses and individuals being willing to borrow at low interest rates and invest. When corporate profits are slim and individuals face the risk of unemployment, even if the cost of borrowing decreases, few people are willing to increase their debt—this is what is known as a “balance sheet recession.”

Shift in Consumption and Investment Expectations

Currently, signs of stagnation have appeared, mainly reflected in the change in people’s expectations for the future. Many people no longer expect promotions and salary increases; this change in expectation directly leads to a contraction in consumption and investment.

Real estate, as the core pillar of the Chinese economy, is unlikely to be re-driven by this round of stimulus. The reason is that market expectations have undergone a profound shift, and the bursting of the bubble has become a reality.

Changes in the Real Estate Market

In the past, people were willing to leverage their “six wallets” (meaning pooling money from multiple family members) to purchase homes, not merely because housing was a basic necessity. Besides basic living needs, almost nothing is an absolute necessity. At that time, housing possessed strong financial attributes, and people generally believed that housing prices would continue to rise, meaning investing in real estate could bring generous returns. Therefore, they viewed home buying not as a liability, but rather as a guaranteed profitable investment. Looking at historical data, the national average housing price rose from 500 yuan per square meter to 20,000 yuan, confirming that past investments yielded returns. However, the current market logic has fundamentally changed.

Conclusion

In summary, I believe the effect of this round of economic stimulus policy will be quite limited. The real estate market will remain sluggish, and after a brief frenzy, the stock market may quickly return to calm, with the index potentially falling below 3,000 points again. The long-term economic challenges still exist, and this stimulus is unlikely to fundamentally reverse the situation.

item.title: Producer Surplus and Consumer Surplus
item.description:
When discussing economics, Producer Surplus is an important concept. It refers to the difference between the actual income received by a producer or supplier when selling goods in the market at a certain price, and the minimum income they expected when willing to sell those goods at that price.

Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:

Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.

When discussing economics, Producer Surplus is an important concept. It refers to the difference between the actual income received by a producer or supplier when selling goods in the market at a certain price, and the minimum income they expected when willing to sell those goods at that price.

Simply put, Producer Surplus is the net gain of the producer in a transaction. Its calculation involves two key factors:

Producer’s Supply Price: This refers to the price at which the producer is willing to sell the goods or services. Typically, the producer’s supply price is related to their marginal cost (the extra cost of producing one unit of goods), because they hope to at least cover the production cost.

Market Price: This refers to the price the buyer is willing to pay, which is the market price of the goods or services.

The calculation formula for Producer Surplus is as follows:

Producer Surplus = Producer’s Supply Price - Market Price

Producer Surplus represents the net gain obtained by the producer when selling goods at a lower supply price. Producer Surplus occurs when the market price is higher than the producer’s supply price, because the producer sells the goods at a lower price but receives a higher actual income. If the market price is lower than the producer’s supply price, the Producer Surplus will be negative, meaning the producer may incur a loss in the transaction.

Producer Surplus is very important for understanding market operation and the supply-demand relationship. In a free market, the balance of supply and demand determines the market price, and Producer Surplus helps us understand the producer’s profitability at different price levels. When the market is in equilibrium, Producer Surplus is maximized, meaning the producer achieves maximum profit.

Okay, Consumer Surplus is an economic term that refers to the economic benefit or value obtained by consumers when purchasing goods or services. Its calculation method is:

Consumer Surplus = Consumer’s Reservation Price (Expected Price) - Actual Paid Price

For a simple example, assume the reservation price for an item is 100 Yuan for the consumer. If the actual market price is 80 Yuan, then the Consumer Surplus obtained by that consumer when purchasing the item is 100 - 80 = 20 Yuan.

Consumer Surplus reflects the net gain obtained by the consumer after purchasing goods or services. The larger the Consumer Surplus, the higher the economic utility obtained by the consumer. Increasing Consumer Surplus can usually raise total social welfare. The government employs many measures to increase Consumer Surplus, such as subsidies, tax incentives, etc.

item.title: What should I do if I want to earn profit beyond the value of the labor itself?
item.description: In a free competitive market, when the wage level of a certain profession or industry is higher than the value deserved by the labor output or skills for that job, it attracts more people to study that profession and enter that market. As the supply increases, the number of workers in the market grows, which subsequently causes the wage level to decrease, eventually approaching the value deserved by the labor output.
item.content:encoded:
In a free competitive market, when the wage level of a certain profession or industry is higher than the value deserved by the labor output or skills for that job, it attracts more people to study that profession and enter that market. As the supply increases, the number of workers in the market grows, which subsequently causes the wage level to decrease, eventually approaching the value deserved by the labor output.

This phenomenon is known in economics as the “Marginal Productivity Theory.” It posits that there is a relationship between the wage level and the marginal output of labor (which is the increase in output generated by adding one unit of labor). When a certain profession’s wage is higher than its marginal output, it attracts more people to join, thereby increasing the labor supply, which in turn lowers the wage level until the marginal output and the wage level reach equilibrium.

This phenomenon is common across many professions and industries. When supply and demand in the market tend towards equilibrium, the wage level usually tends towards the value of the marginal output—this is the situation you mentioned where profit approaches zero. In the long run, the market forms a relatively stable equilibrium state, and the wage level adjusts to match the skills, labor output, and market demand.

This also explains why continuous learning and skill improvement are extremely important for individuals to achieve success and obtain better compensation in the workplace. By constantly improving one’s skills and knowledge, an individual can maintain competitiveness in a fierce market and achieve better economic returns.

If you wish to earn extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself in the labor market, you can consider the following strategies:

Differentiation and Specialization: Find the field or specific skill you excel in, and continuously refine it to become an expert. Through differentiation and specialization, you can provide higher quality and more specialized services, thereby creating higher market value for yourself.

Creating Unique Value: Identify the pain points or needs in the market and provide unique solutions. Understand the customer’s true needs and offer services that exceed their expectations. This can win you more customers and positive word-of-mouth, leading to extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself.

Building a Personal Brand: Establish your visibility and authority in the industry through effective branding and personal promotion. A reputable and credible personal brand can bring you more business opportunities and chances, potentially leading to higher returns.

Mastering Composite Skills: Learning and mastering skills across multiple fields allows you to become a versatile individual. Possessing multiple skills increases your flexibility and adaptability, better meeting market demands, which brings you more opportunities and potential profits.

Innovation and Leadership: Continuously innovating and leading teams to achieve goals can bring you more business opportunities and project collaborations, thereby creating extra profit for you.

It is important to emphasize that pursuing extra profit beyond the value of the labor itself is not easy; it requires a significant investment of time, effort, and resources. Furthermore, success is not achieved overnight; it requires continuous effort and ongoing learning and growth. The key is to find the development path and strategy that suits you and continuously optimize and adjust it through practice. In a fiercely competitive market, only by continuously enhancing your value can you gain more opportunities and profits in the workplace.

item.title: Holy Book *Naval Compendium: Guide to Wealth and Happiness*
item.description: Naval Ravikant's profound insights on wealth, knowledge, decision-making, and happiness, helping you build a more successful and fulfilling life.
item.content:encoded:
1. People Should Seek Wealth, Not Money or Status

People should not earn wealth through arduous work. Working 80 hours a week in a restaurant will not make you richer. Hard work is unavoidable, but it should be done in the right way. People should seek wealth, not money or status. If you believe wealth is unimportant, wealth will move away from you. Wealth is assets that continue to make money while you sleep. Without wealth-generating assets, when you sleep, you have no income; when you retire, you cannot keep earning money. In short, without wealth, you cannot achieve non-linear earning. Generally, wealth is created by starting your own company or by investing. Neither of these is achieved by putting in a massive amount of time; the ultra-rich, just like you, only have 24 hours every day.

2. The Key to Acquiring Wealth

To acquire wealth, you can provide something valuable to the masses—especially something they don’t know how to obtain. And you must supply it on a large scale. The internet has greatly expanded career possibilities, and most people still lack a clear understanding of this. Learn marketing, learn creation. If you master these two things, nothing can stop you from succeeding.

3. Arm Yourself with Special Knowledge

Special knowledge is knowledge that cannot be acquired through training. If it can be acquired through training, others can also acquire it, and they can replace you. Special knowledge is usually high in technical sophistication and creative. It cannot be outsourced or automated. (For example, insight) It can be discovered when driven by genuine curiosity and passion. The process of creating special knowledge feels like playing to you, but like working to others. Usually, special knowledge lies at the boundaries of knowledge—things that are either newly understood or genuinely difficult to understand. If you do not commit 100%, someone who commits 100% will surpass you. And they won’t just be slightly better; they will be much better, because in the realm of ideas, compound interest will work, and leverage will work. Special knowledge might be things like: Sales skills. Having musical talent. Persistence: This means you can research things with dedication. Loving science fiction: This means you can quickly absorb a lot of knowledge. Playing many games: This means you have a good understanding of game theory. Gossip: This might help you become a very interesting journalist. Special knowledge is a strange combination, coming from your DNA, your unique environment of growth, and your response to that knowledge. These are almost integrated into your personality and identity, and then you can continuously refine them. Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, brainwashing techniques, ethics, mathematics, and computer science.

4. Arm Yourself with Leverage

Business leverage mainly consists of capital, labor, and products with extremely low replication costs (code and media). Capital refers to money. To raise funds, you need to use your special knowledge, combined with your sense of responsibility, to demonstrate your good judgment. Labor refers to the people who work for you. It is the oldest and most fiercely contested form of leverage. Labor leverage will make your parents feel proud, but don’t waste your life pursuing this alone. Capital and labor are forms of leverage that require permission to use. Everyone chases capital, but there must always be someone to pay for it. Everyone wants to lead others, but there must always be subordinates. Code and media are forms of leverage that require no permission; they are the leverage behind the new rich. You can create software and media that work for you even while you sleep. A large group of robots is available for free use—to save space and energy efficiency, they are packaged into data centers; use them! By applying special knowledge combined with leverage, you will ultimately get what you deserve.

5. In One Sentence: Productize Yourself

What does this mean? “Productize” and “yourself.” “Yourself” has uniqueness; “productize” has leverage. “Am I productizing it? Can I scale it? Can I amplify it through labor, capital, code, or media?” So, this phrase is very easy to remember. If you want to be richer, you must figure out what you can provide to society that society doesn’t know how to obtain, but that society wants, and providing it to you is natural and within your skill set and capability. Next, you must find a way to scale it, because producing only one is far from enough. You might need to produce thousands, or tens of thousands, or millions, or even billions, so that everyone can have one. Steve Jobs (and his team, of course) figured out that society needed a smartphone. This smartphone had all the functions of phones at the time, but also many other new functions, and it was easier to use. Therefore, they figured out how to manufacture the smartphone, and then they figured out how to mass-produce the smartphone. You must become the person who can scale the provision of these products or services. This is the real challenge of how to make money.

6. Pay Attention to Your Character

In my life, I have known some extremely successful, very popular, and very smart people. However, I have seen them do one or two things that were not very good for others. I would say, “Hey, I think you shouldn’t do this to others. Because it will ultimately hurt yourself.” Deep down, we all know who we are. You cannot hide anything from yourself. You are very clear whether what you do is right or wrong; if you have too many moral flaws, you will not respect yourself. The worst outcome in this world is a lack of self-respect. If you don’t love yourself, who will love you? If I see someone doing this, the first time I will remind them, but usually they won’t change, and then I will keep my distance from them. I cut them out of my life. If someone constantly claims to be honest, they are likely dishonest. These are just some effective indicators that I have learned. When someone spends a lot of time talking about their values or talking about themselves, it means they are hiding something. I think to myself: “If you want to get close to me, your values must be better than mine.”

7. Smart People Truly Understand One Thing

If someone uses many complex words and many grand concepts, they are likely unaware of what they are actually talking about. I believe the smartest people can explain things to a child. If you cannot explain it to a child, then you don’t truly know it. Truly smart thinkers are clear-thinking thinkers; they understand very, very basic foundational knowledge.

8. Step Outside Yourself to See the Truth

Imagine one of my friends is going through some difficulties, such as a breakup, career issues, business failure, or health problems. When he needs my advice, it often takes me only a few minutes to accurately tell him, “Oh, that girl, forget her. Anyway, she’s not good for you. You will be happier. Believe me. You will find someone more suitable in the future.” But he himself finds it difficult to see this. Because he is in pain and torment, his desires conflict with reality, which prevents him from seeing the truth clearly. The same thing happens when we make decisions. To see the truth clearly, you must set aside the self, because the self does not want to face the truth.

9. What is Truly Important is Leisure Time

Great ideas only come after you feel bored. Good ideas never appear when you are under pressure, busy, rushing around, or in a hurry. If your schedule doesn’t have one or two days a week where you aren’t constantly in meetings or constantly busy, you cannot think. You won’t have good ideas related to your business. You also cannot make good judgments. I encourage you to set aside at least one day a week (better yet, two days, because if you prepare two days, you will definitely find one) so that you have time to think. Cherish your time; it is everything. It is more important than your money. It is more important than your friends. It is more important than anything. Your time is everything. Don’t waste your time.

10. Reading Can Make You Successful

Spending one hour a day reading science, mathematics, and philosophy can likely put you on the high ladder of human success within seven years. I have spent a lot of time reading. My only true friend is books. Books are great friends because they tell you the wisdom of the best thinkers over the past thousands of years. Any book that has survived for two thousand years has been screened by many people, and it is more likely to be correct; I want to reread these books. The fact is, I read not for self-improvement. I read out of curiosity and interest. The best book is the one that captivates you.

11. Do Things for Your Own Goals

I truly want to do things for my own goals. Whether it is business, fitness, romance, friendship, or anything else, I believe the meaning of life is to do things for your own goals. When you do things for yourself, you can create your best work. Even if you do these things to make money, you will actually be the most successful. Follow your true curiosity, not the current hot topics. If your curiosity leads you to where society will eventually go, you will receive rich rewards. When you are dating, there is a moment you realize that the relationship will not lead to marriage, you might be better off moving on. When you are learning something, such as geography or history, and you realize you will never use this information, drop that course. That is wasting time. That is wasting mental energy.

12. Become a Better Decision-Maker Overall

Become a better decision-maker overall. Decision-making is everything. Yes. Decision-making is everything. In fact, someone who makes correct decisions 80% of the time instead of 70% of the time will have value and compensation in the market hundreds of times higher. I believe people find it difficult to understand a basic fact of leverage. If I manage $1 billion, and I am often 10% more correct than others, my decisions can bring $100 million in value in a single judgment. With modern technology, massive labor, and capital, the multiplier of our decisions can be leveraged to increasingly higher levels. If I face a difficult choice, such as these questions: Should I marry this person? Should I take this job? Should I buy this house? Should I move to this city? Should I partner with this person in business? If you cannot decide, answer no. The reason is that modern society is full of choices. There are so many choices. We live on a planet with 7 billion people, and we can connect with everyone through the internet. There are hundreds of thousands of professions for you to choose from. There are so many choices. When you choose certain things, you are locked in for a very long time. Starting a business might take 10 years. Starting a relationship might take 5 years or more. Moving to a city might take 10 to 20 years. These are all decisions with very, very long-term impact. We only say “yes” when we are very certain. You can never be absolutely certain, but you must be very confident. If you have two choices, and they are relatively equal, then choose the path that is more difficult and more painful in the short term. The reality is that one path will endure short-term pain. The other path will feel pain further down the line in the future. However, your brain tries to avoid conflict and tries to avoid short-term pain. By definition, if two choices are similar, and one has short-term pain, then this choice is related to long-term gain. According to the law of compound interest, long-term gain is what you want. Your brain overvalues short-term happiness and tries to avoid short-term pain. Caffeine is another thing that trades long-term consequences for short-term benefits. Essentially, you must, through your life, replace bad habits you unconsciously acquire with good habits, committing to become a happier person.

13. On Happiness

Confucius said that a person has two lives, and the second life begins when you realize that life is only one. So, when and how does your second life begin? (Confucius said: I never said that.) I read a quote by Blaise Pascal. It roughly means: “All of humanity’s unhappiness is because they cannot sit quietly in their rooms.” If you sit for 30 minutes and feel happy, you are successful. This is a very high state, but few people achieve it. The core skill you must learn is to be content with circumstances and go with the flow in most situations. You can get almost anything you want from life, as long as it is what you want the most. The first rule of handling conflict is: don’t be with people who frequently cause conflict. I am not interested in things that are not sustainable or difficult to sustain, including relationships full of problems.

14. The Top Priority of Life

The top priority of my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my own health. First is my physical health. Second is my mental health. Third is my spiritual health. After that, is my family’s health. After that, is my family’s happiness. After that, I can do anything else in the world that I need to do. Basically, whenever you recommend a good habit to someone, they will find an excuse for themselves, and the most common excuse is usually, “I don’t have time.” When you hear this, you know they are saying, “This is not a high-priority matter.” If something is your top priority, you will do it. That is how life works. If you have 10 to 15 vague and non-urgent matters, you will ultimately not do any of them. What I do is decide that the top priority in my life, above my happiness, above my family, above my work, is my health. My physical health has become my top priority, so I can never say I don’t have time. In the morning, I exercise, no matter how long it takes, I insist on exercising. If I haven’t finished exercising, I won’t start the day’s work. I don’t care if the world is collapsing and melting; it can wait another 30 minutes until I finish exercising. Just like other things in life, if you are willing to make short-term sacrifices, you will have long-term benefits. “Easy choice, difficult life. Difficult choice, easy life.”

15. Don’t Fight Your Own Thoughts

Don’t take yourself too seriously. You are just a monkey with a plan. Don’t make any decisions, don’t make any judgments; just accept everything. If I walk and do this for ten to fifteen minutes, I enter a very calm, grateful state. Non-judgmental consciousness is very useful to me. Another method I learned is to sit there, close my eyes, for at least an hour every day. You surrender to whatever happens—without effort. You don’t strive to do certain things, nor do you strive to oppose certain things. If thoughts flow through your mind, you flow with those thoughts. “If a thought comes, a thought comes. I don’t fight it. I don’t embrace it. I don’t think about it. I don’t reject it. I just sit there with my eyes closed for an hour, doing nothing.” This is a state of happiness, bliss, and tranquility. Once you have it, you don’t want to give it up. If you can gain an hour of happy freedom time just by sitting with your eyes closed every morning, that is priceless. It will change your life. All you have to do is sit there and do nothing. Just sit down. Close your eyes and say: “I just want to rest for an hour. This is an hour away from life, an hour where I do nothing.”

16. Let Consciousness and Mind Coexist Harmoniously

Buddhists talk about consciousness and the self; they truly view your brain as a multi-layered mechanism: a core-level operating system is running, and then there are some applications running on top of it. I am returning to the operating system of my consciousness layer, which is always calm, always peaceful, usually happy and satisfied. I try to maintain this state instead of activating the “monkey mind” (referring to the mind below consciousness). The monkey mind is always worried, afraid, and anxious; it has incredible power, but I try not to activate it until I need it. If I run it non-stop for 24 hours, I will waste energy, and the monkey mind will become me; I am more important than my monkey mind. The mind itself is a muscle—it can be trained and regulated, but it has been haphazardly trained by society into a form that we cannot control. If you examine your mind with consciousness and intention, I think you can extract your own thoughts, emotions, ideas, and reactions, and then you can start reprogramming. You can rewrite this program according to your will.

17. How to Define Wisdom?

A person understands the long-term consequences of what they do.

What? Are Money Values Tiered?

Does the money of the rich hold more value than the money of the ordinary person? Why is that? Is it because the rich spend money better than the ordinary person? Or is it because they possess some special investment strategy? In this article, we will explore the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, and provide some practical suggestions to help ordinary people achieve wealth growth.

The Money of the Rich Has Potential Growth Value

Let’s start with a simple example. Suppose both the rich and the ordinary person have 10,000 yuan. For the ordinary person, this 10,000 yuan might be used for daily expenses, such as clothes, pants, bags, rent, or mortgage payments. Although these expenses are necessary, they do not generate any additional income. In contrast, the rich person’s 10,000 yuan might be invested in stocks, bonds, real estate, etc. While these investments carry a certain risk, they can also bring substantial returns.

For example, suppose the rich person invests 10,000 yuan in a stock with an annualized return rate of 10%. Then, next year, this 10,000 yuan will become 11,000 yuan, and the year after, it will become 12,100 yuan, and so on. This potential growth value makes the rich person’s money more valuable than the ordinary person’s money.

The Rich Spend Money More Prudently

So, why are the rich more cautious when spending money? It is because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending, including the impact on future income. For the rich, spending 10,000 yuan is not just spending 10,000 yuan; it means giving up potential investment returns. Therefore, they consider the necessity and potential consequences of spending more carefully.

For instance, suppose the rich person needs to buy a new car. They might consider factors such as the car’s price, fuel efficiency, maintenance costs, and compare it with other investment opportunities. They might ask themselves:

  • Is this car worth spending so much money on?
  • Are there better investment opportunities?

This cautious attitude makes the rich more rational and prudent in their spending.

Spending Ratio of the Rich vs. Ordinary People

So, what is the difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary person? According to research, the income of the ordinary person is often entirely used for expenses, while the spending ratio of the rich is extremely low. For example, suppose the ordinary person’s monthly income is 5,000 yuan, and they might use their entire income for expenses, such as rent, mortgage, and living costs. In contrast, the rich person’s monthly income might be 50,000 yuan, but their spending ratio might only be 1%. This means they have more money available for investment and savings.

Conclusion

By exploring the differences between the money of the rich and the ordinary, we found that the rich person’s money is more valuable because it has potential growth value. We also found that the rich are more prudent when spending, because they need to consider the potential consequences of spending. Finally, we learned that there is a significant difference in the spending ratio between the rich and the ordinary.

Recommendations

So, how can ordinary people achieve wealth growth by changing their spending habits and investment strategies? Here are some practical suggestions:

  • Start Investing: Consider using your money for investment. How to invest is another serious topic.
  • Reduce Expenses: Try to reduce your spending ratio, leaving more money for investment and savings.
  • Spend Prudently: When spending, consider the potential consequences of the expenditure, including the impact on future income.

By taking these measures, ordinary people can begin to achieve wealth growth and make their money more valuable.
